concerns: The proposed national contrast is misleading for everyday usage because memakai is also very common in Indonesian for wearing clothing.
response.cue_rationale: Both mengenakan and memakai can mean wearing clothing on the body.
material_concerns: The pair presents mengenakan as an Indonesian everyday counterpart to Malaysian memakai, although Indonesian commonly uses memakai for this same sense; mengenakan is more formal.

preference_risk.rationale: Memakai is plausibly ordinary for wearing clothing in both varieties, undermining the proposed Indonesian-versus-Malaysian preference.

response.rationale: Both forms fit the sense of having clothing on the body, but the proposed contrast is not a reliable everyday Indonesian–Malaysian distinction. Indonesian memakai is common, while mengenakan is comparatively formal.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: Memakai is an ordinary everyday form for this sense in both Indonesian and Malaysian, so it weakens the claimed national preference.
